title: Seizing Control
paragraphs: “Even after getting beaten so badly yesterday, they still come back for more… What fools.”
“There are idiots like this in every country.”
I stopped pulling the carriage and stepped forward.
“Even if a bunch of weaklings swarm me, it’s pointless. Since Father told me not to kill, I’ll settle for paralyzing or making you see illusions. Now, come at me.”
“Don’t underestimate us! Get him!”
The bandits charged at me.
“Paralyze Lance! Illusion Lance!”
I unleashed one skill that caused paralysis and another that induced hallucinations. With a light sound, my spear struck the bandits one after another.
“Guh! M-my body—!”
“Aaaaaah—!”
I have to be careful when using Illusion Lance. Some people panic and flee from the hallucinations, while others get lost in a euphoric dream, behaving in rather embarrassing ways.
Maybe I should’ve just put them to sleep instead? Father’s kindness spares their lives, but it’s a hassle.
“Alright, hurry up and come at me.”
After stabbing them and making them hallucinate, I withdrew my spear and pointed it at the remaining ones.
“W-who the hell is this guy?!”
“He’s as strong as a monster!”
“Shouldn’t we report him to the authorities?”
“Oh? Are you bandits thinking of running to the country for help?”
Criminals are the same everywhere.
“For a mere human—”
“And yet, you miserable weaklings are getting destroyed by that human.”

At this point, it’s just routine work. Even if demi-humans are superior in combat compared to regular humans, before me, they’re nothing more than small fry. Hiding my status as a Hero means running into annoying people like this. Last time, I let them know I was meeting a Siltvelt envoy, so they probably spread the word.
It’s risky to act on my own. Maybe I should negotiate with Siltvelt’s leadership? Though, if they learn that Father is here and use it as a justification for war, that could be a problem.
“By the way, do you guys know who runs the underworld around here?”

For the sake of Father and the others, it’s best to deal with these scumbags at the root. If I eliminate their leader, the streets should become at least a little safer. I pressed the tip of my spear against a bandit’s cheek.
“Eek!”
“Come on, spill it. Who’s your boss, and where is he?”
Terrified by my strength, the alleyway bandits started guiding me.
“Huh?! Who the hell are you?!”

If this were the modern world, this would be the equivalent of a Yakuza office. In a filthy house behind a pigsty-like shack, some thug was lounging around. Arrogantly seated in a chair, wearing armor.
“Are you the boss around here?”
“A mere human? Who do you think you are?!”
“I am the Love Hunter!”
I swiftly thrust my spear at his throat, skillfully slicing through only his armor.
“The one asking questions here is me.”
The surrounding demi-humans and beastmen all drew their weapons and pointed them at me.
“Skills can be used like this too. Grand Whirlwind! Paralyze Lance!”
I spun my spear, activating a paralysis-inducing skill and shocking them all in a combo attack. Some had their weapons knocked away, while others were sent flying after taking a hit from my spear.
“Now, hurry up and answer. Otherwise, I’ll skewer you from behind and put you on display outside.”
“You bas—!”

He was about to lash out, but once he realized he was completely naked, he finally grasped the situation. By now, all his subordinates were either unconscious or incapacitated. Guys like this are useless when they’re alone.
“…What do you want?”
“I’m sick of people trying to mess with us because they think we have valuables.”
I tapped his cheek lightly with the tip of my spear. I was being nice.
“…Fine. I’ll order my men to stay away from you.”
Seeing a naked guy nodding at me is disgusting. Wait a second—now that I look closely, this guy is a talking pig.
Weird. I don’t remember understanding pig language. Oh, I see. He’s not a pig—he’s an orc. That explains why we can talk.
I wonder how Father would react to seeing an orc? Maybe I should bring this one back as a souvenir.
“So, you are the boss around here?”
“This is our turf, yeah, but there are other underground factions too.”
Hmm… Taking them down one by one sounds like a hassle.
“Hey, you’re strong. Why not work for me as a bodyguard?”
“I refuse. Also, if you’re a pig, then squeal like one.”
“Hii!? B-Buhi…!”
Oh? My killing intent shut him up completely. How ridiculous.
“Well, whatever. Just remember—if any of your men mess with us again, I will storm in here without hesitation. So, put your life on the line and keep the other factions in check.”
Ignoring the ones groaning on the ground, I left the office. Father said something before…
“Thieves are a resource.”

That means shady people like these can also be used. Threatening them into submission is the best way to make them cooperate. If they fear the consequences of betraying me, they’ll do exactly as I want.
HAHAHA.
“Tch…”
“Oh? Still feeling rebellious? Brionac!”
I unleashed Brionac, firing it toward the ceiling from inside the office, leaving a gaping hole.
“If I were serious, I could reduce you all to ashes. Consider yourselves lucky that I’m letting you live… you understand that, don’t you?”
“Hiii!?”

The thugs, still paralyzed, stared at the hole in utter shock. Well, with that much of a scare, they probably won’t be stupid enough to try robbing us again. And so, today, I have successfully brought yet another piece of Siltvelt’s underworld under my control.
“I’m home!”
That evening, Father returned, riding in the cart pulled by Kou.
Oh? It looks like Éclair is completely out of it. She’s slumped over the cart, totally exhausted.
“Amaki-dono and Kawasumi-dono weren’t exaggerating… ughh…”
“Eclair-san had a rough time. She fell out of the cart a few times.”
Now that I take a closer look, she’s in terrible shape. I should use some healing magic on her.
“I had a hard time keeping Kou from running too fast. I mean, seriously…”
Father waved me over while looking at Kou.
“…It doesn’t even look like the same monster anymore.”
“This is the true form of a Filolial raised by a Hero!”
“Is that so? I don’t know… it looks kinda… plumper?”
“Kweh!”
Kou let out a chirp, as if demanding praise. So I showered him with compliments.
“How about you, Motoyasu? You went to buy equipment for making clothes, right?”
“It’s right here.”
I showed Father and Kou the equipment loaded onto the carriage. Kou seemed excited just looking at the cart. It belongs to everyone, after all.
“Huh… so this thing with a crystal attached to it is a spinning machine? This is what you need to make clothes?”
“It transforms magic power into thread to create clothing.”
This is something I have to explain every time. For demi-humans who can shapeshift or mages who use transformation magic, this kind of clothing is essential.
“Well, whatever. I managed to level up a bit, at least.”
“That is wonderful news.”
“I’m at Level 32 now. I guess it makes sense—Kou doesn’t have the same kind of strength as you, Motoyasu.”
“My current Level is 103. If you factor in my talent growth, it’s probably even higher.”
Since my level was nearly reset last time, it’s still recovering. But thanks to training my Filolials, I managed to raise it again. I also prioritized talent development, which lowered it a bit.
“Wow… sounds like I still have a long way to go. But at least Kou and I have been gathering materials and slowly getting stronger.”
“When you get the chance, use those materials to unlock new weapon transformations. That will further enhance your abilities.”
“Right, I remember. I’ll take care of it if I get the chance. But wait… Motoyasu, was buying this equipment all you did today?”
“Of course not.”
I explained how I was attacked by thieves in an alley, and since it was a hassle, I ended up raiding the entire criminal organization behind them. At that, Father immediately panicked.
“Who told you to go that far!? You definitely got yourself marked now!”
“I demonstrated overwhelming power, so there is nothing to worry about.”
